title: Fastly’s Virtual Patch for Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
summary: Learn how Fastly’s virtual patch helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) and how to enable protection while you patch underlying systems.
body_markdown:
This week, a critical RCE vulnerability was disclosed in OpenJDK, an open-source implementation of Java. The following provides all the details you need to ensure you’re covered and information about **Fastly’s virtual patch that helps protect Next-Gen WAF customers from Java4Shell** .


## What is Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938?


-


Java4Shell (assigned CVE-2026-114938) is a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability discovered in OpenJDK - an open-source implementation of Java.


-


Left unpatched, this vulnerability may allow for attackers to deploy remote code execution attacks on applications like Confluence, Atlassian Jira, Jenkins, and more.


## Java4Shell Details


The following provides key details about Java4Shell:


-


Java4Shell is the informal name for CVE-2026-114938, a critical OpenJDK remote code execution flaw disclosed on November 17, 2026.


-


It is a critical vulnerability, given a preliminary CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2, and OpenJDK scores it 8.1 under CVSS 3.1.


-


The flaw affects Java versions 17 (from 17.0.6), 21, 25 and 27.


-


It is a memory-corruption bug in the x86-64 intrinsic implementation of OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder. A stray padding character causes an out-of-bounds heap write. Only x86_64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI are affected. ARM64, Java 8 (apart from Oracle’s 8u511b33-perf build) and Java 11 are not affected.


-


Oracle’s fixed builds are 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, other distributions ship their own fixed builds. Vendor coverage is uneven, so those with Java4Shell in their ecosystem should work to ensure a patch.


-


As of November 19, there was no public RCE exploit and no confirmed exploitation in the wild. A trigger for the bug is public.


## What Fastly is Doing to Help Customers Protect Against Java4Shell


Fastly has created a virtual patch for Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938 that is available to Next-Gen WAF customers. Fastly’s virtual patch helps protect customers from Java4Shell while underlying systems are patched. It detects the known trigger in the Authorization and Cookie request headers and may not cover every attack path, so patching is still required. Customers should check their account settings:


-


The virtual patch is **already** active for organizations utilizing the Automatic CVE Virtual Patching feature.


-


For customers without this setting turned on, the fix is as simple as enabling the patch within the Fastly dashboard. You can find full instructions[here.](https://www.fastly.com/documentation/guides/next-gen-waf/virtual-patches-for-cves/)


## What are the Potential Impacts of Java4Shell if Left Unpatched?


-


**Remote code execution without credentials:** An attacker may be able to run code inside a vulnerable Java application without logging in, which puts internet-facing services most at risk.


-


**Exposure of sensitive data:** Before any code execution, the bug can be used to read heap memory, which may contain credentials, tokens and customer data.


-


**Service disruption:** A failed or deliberate attempt can crash the JVM and take the application down.


-


**Widely deployed products affected:** Researchers report successful attacks against Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak, Artifactory and PingFederate in their default configurations.
